rewrites.//: A form's link (MS-360). /f/<token> is what goes in a text message to the whole church, and it has to look like something a person would tap — but the token is 128 bits of base58 and never the form's title, because a readable slug is a guessable one and would make every public form enumerable (ADR-0051). The page reads the token off the path; ?f=<token> still works so links copied from an older build do not break.

headers.//: Firebase's default is an hour's cache on everything. Nothing here is content-hashed — calendar.js is always calendar.js — so for an hour after a deploy a browser can run the NEW page against the OLD script. Alpine swallows a binding to a member the old script never had, so the symptom is a screen that renders blank rather than an error: exactly the bug that hid this. ⚠ THIS COSTS A FULL RE-DOWNLOAD PER FILE, NOT A 304 — see the vendor block below. It is still right for these files, which genuinely can go stale; the way out is giving them a name that changes when they do, and then they can be cached like everything else.

⚠ no-cache DOES NOT COST ONE 304 PER FILE ON THIS HOST. That is what the block above assumed, and it is wrong: asked about a no-cache file the browser already holds, Firebase Hosting sends the whole body back rather than 'nothing changed'. Measured against the live site — firebase-firestore-compat.js answers a conditional request with 200 and 84KB, while a font on max-age answers the same question with 304 and nothing. So every page visit re-downloaded ~200KB the browser was already holding, which on a phone was most of the wait before the page could even ask for its data. Third-party code is exempted here because it has the property the block above is missing: it changes name when it changes. alpine-3.15.12.min.js carries its version, and the Firebase files only move when somebody vendors a new SDK. That is ~128KB of the ~200. ⚠ IT MUST STAY BELOW THE no-cache BLOCK. The LAST matching block wins, not the first — put this above it and vendor/ silently keeps no-cache. Verified against the hosting emulator, not assumed.
Fonts and images ARE stable — a woff2 that changes gets a new name.

hosting.//: The Order of Service MCP server (MS-262, ADR-0038) gets its OWN hosting site, and that is not tidiness — it is required. The OAuth discovery specs put /authorize, /token, /register and /revoke at the ROOT of whatever origin serves them, so hosting this on the church domain would claim all four there. Everything below is a rewrite to the single `mcp` function; mcp-site/ holds only a placeholder page for anyone who visits the bare domain. ⚠ The origin here must match MCP_ISSUER_URL in functions/index.js exactly — it is the issuer clients pin to and the audience every access token is minted for, so a mismatch means either nothing connects or passes minted elsewhere are accepted.

functions.//: predeploy copies the pure domain modules the server shares with the browser into functions/shared. functions/ deploys as its own bundle and cannot require across into public/, and MS-20 needs RolesCore server-side to refuse an ineligible member (ADR-0030). One authored copy lives in public/; test/functions-shared-sync.test.js fails if the copy here is stale, so this hook is a safety net rather than the only thing keeping them in step.
